text: You just slammed your leg into the coffee table, and by tomorrow it's purple.
The hit breaks tiny blood vessels under your skin, and blood leaks out.
That trapped blood is the bruise. Fresh, it's red, then it turns blue and purple.
Your body breaks the blood down, so it turns green, then yellow, and fades in about two weeks.
So why do some people bruise so easily?
As you get older, your skin gets thinner, with less padding over those vessels.
Aspirin and blood thinners can do it too. Big bruises for no reason? See a doctor.
Tag the friend who's always covered in bruises, and subscribe.
